page_performance_surface_label: Example State official voter-information page-performance policy
delivery_role_note: Performance review helps keep current official voter-information pages usable on ordinary mobile conditions, but it does not replace content correctness, accessibility, or the current office/help lane as the authority source.
mobile_first_scope_note: Critical voter-task pages are reviewed as mobile-first public-service paths because the public often reaches them from phones under time pressure.
field_data_note: Real-user field posture is reviewed separately from release-preflight checks so the office does not confuse green lab runs with actual public experience.
lab_preflight_note: Template, CMS, script, banner, and localization changes run through a bounded preflight review for the critical page classes before release.
performance_budget_note: The office keeps declared budgets and release thresholds for critical page classes and treats over-budget regressions as block, rollback, or waiver decisions rather than as post-hoc debate.
hydration_boundary_note: Major answer text and the office/help recovery lane should remain reachable even when richer widgets or client-side hydration degrade.
release_gate_note: Critical-page regressions beyond declared thresholds trigger a release hold or a time-bounded waiver with an explicit fallback plan.
fallback_behavior_note: When richer UI degrades, the office preserves a plain-language current answer and a stable office/help route rather than leaving a blank or spinner-only shell.
